name_translation: The Yoga of the Divine and Demonic Natures

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिर्ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः |
दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् || १ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिर्ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः |
दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
abhayaṃ sattvasaṃśuddhirjñānayogavyavasthitiḥ |
dānaṃ damaśca yajñaśca svādhyāyastapa ārjavam || 1 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; abhayam—fearlessness; sattva-saṃśuddhiḥ—purity of inner heart/being; jñāna-yoga-vyavasthitiḥ—steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge; dānam—charity/generosity; damaḥ ca—and control of the outer senses; yajñaḥ ca—and performance of selfless sacrifice; svādhyāyaḥ—study of sacred scriptures; tapaḥ—austerity/discipline; ārjavam—straightforwardness and simplicity.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge, charity, sense-control, performance of sacrifice, study of the sacred scriptures, austerity, and straightforwardness;
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna begins by enumerating the 26 divine virtues (Daivi Sampad). 'Abhayam' (fearlessness arising from absolute faith in God) is the primary foundation, followed by inner mental clarity, selfless giving, self-restraint, scriptural contemplation, and moral integrity.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna begins by enumerating the 26 divine virtues (Daivi Sampad). 'Abhayam' (fearlessness arising from absolute faith in God) is the primary foundation, followed by inner mental clarity, selfless giving, self-restraint, scriptural contemplation, and moral integrity.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् |
दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् || २ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् |
दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ahiṃsā satyamakrodhastyāgaḥ śāntirapaiśunam |
dayā bhūteṣvaloluptvaṃ mārdavaṃ hrīracāpalam || 2 ||
verses.word_meanings: ahiṃsā—non-violence; satyam—truthfulness; akrodhaḥ—freedom from anger; tyāgaḥ—renunciation of egoic possessiveness; śāntiḥ—inner tranquility/peace; apaiśunam—aversion to fault-finding and malicious gossip; dayā bhūteṣu—compassion towards all living beings; aloluptvam—freedom from covetousness and greed; mārdavam—gentleness; hrīḥ—modesty/humility; acāpalam—freedom from restlessness/fickleness.
verses.translation: Non-violence, truthfulness, absence of anger, renunciation, tranquility, aversion to slander and fault-finding, compassion toward all living beings, freedom from covetousness, gentleness, modesty, and steady unvacillating determination;
verses.meaning: The second tier of divine qualities focuses on relational harmony and psychological mastery: Ahimsa (causing no harm in thought, word, or deed), Satya (benevolent truth), Akrodha (subduing retaliatory wrath), and universal compassion for all creatures.
verses.purport: The second tier of divine qualities focuses on relational harmony and psychological mastery: Ahimsa (causing no harm in thought, word, or deed), Satya (benevolent truth), Akrodha (subduing retaliatory wrath), and universal compassion for all creatures.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता |
भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत || ३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता |
भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ śaucamadroho nātimānitā |
bhavanti sampadaṃ daivīmabhijātasya bhārata || 3 ||
verses.word_meanings: tejaḥ—vigor/spiritual radiance; kṣamā—forgiveness/patience; dhṛtiḥ—fortitude/perseverance; śaucam—cleanliness of body and mind; adrohaḥ—freedom from malice and envy; na-atimānitā—absence of excessive pride and arrogance; bhavanti—belong to; sampadam daivīm—divine nature/wealth; abhijātasya—of one born endowed with; bhārata—O descendant of Bharata (Arjuna).
verses.translation: Spiritual vigor, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, absence of malice, and freedom from pride—these sublime virtues belong to one born endowed with the divine nature, O descendant of Bharata.
verses.meaning: These 26 attributes comprise 'Daivi Sampad'—the divine treasure that spiritualizes human consciousness, dissolving egoic boundaries and preparing the soul for direct union with the Supreme.
verses.purport: These 26 attributes comprise 'Daivi Sampad'—the divine treasure that spiritualizes human consciousness, dissolving egoic boundaries and preparing the soul for direct union with the Supreme.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च |
अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम् || ४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च |
अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम् || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
dambho darpo'bhimānaśca krodhaḥ pāruṣyameva ca |
ajñānaṃ cābhijātasya pārtha sampadamāsurīm || 4 ||
verses.word_meanings: dambhaḥ—hypocrisy and ostentation; darpaḥ—arrogance and boastfulness; abhimānaḥ ca—and self-conceit; krodhaḥ—wrath/anger; pāruṣyam—harshness and cruelty; eva ca—and also; ajñānam—spiritual ignorance/darkness; ca—and; abhijātasya—of one born endowed with; pārtha—O son of Pritha (Arjuna); sampadam āsurīm—the demonic nature/wealth.
verses.translation: Hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, wrath, harshness, and ignorance—these traits belong to one born endowed with the demonic nature, O Partha.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna immediately contrasts divine virtue with 'Asuri Sampad' (the demonic nature). Its hallmarks are religious pretense (Dambha), haughtiness (Darpa), inflated egoism (Abhimana), abusive temper (Krodha), cruelty in speech and action (Parushyam), and spiritual darkness (Ajnana).
verses.purport: Sri Krishna immediately contrasts divine virtue with 'Asuri Sampad' (the demonic nature). Its hallmarks are religious pretense (Dambha), haughtiness (Darpa), inflated egoism (Abhimana), abusive temper (Krodha), cruelty in speech and action (Parushyam), and spiritual darkness (Ajnana).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता |
मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव || ५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता |
मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
daivī sampadvimokṣāya nibandhāyāsurī matā |
mā śucaḥ sampadaṃ daivīmabhijāto'si pāṇḍava || 5 ||
verses.word_meanings: daivī sampat—the divine nature; vimokṣāya—leads to ultimate liberation (Moksha); nibandhāya—causes perpetual bondage; āsurī—the demonic nature; matā—is regarded; mā śucaḥ—do not grieve / do not despair; sampadam daivīm—with divine endowments; abhijātaḥ asi—you are born; pāṇḍava—O Pandava (Arjuna).
verses.translation: The divine qualities lead to ultimate liberation (Moksha), whereas the demonic traits lead to perpetual bondage. Do not grieve, O Pandava, for you are born endowed with divine qualities.
verses.meaning: Divine virtue liberates the soul by burning away ego and karma; demonic tendencies chain the soul to lower wombs and suffering. Sri Krishna comforts Arjuna with the assurance that his nature is fundamentally saintly and divine.
verses.purport: Divine virtue liberates the soul by burning away ego and karma; demonic tendencies chain the soul to lower wombs and suffering. Sri Krishna comforts Arjuna with the assurance that his nature is fundamentally saintly and divine.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन्दैव आसुर एव च |
दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे शृणु || ६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन्दैव आसुर एव च |
दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे शृणु || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
dvau bhūtasargau loke'smindaiva āsura eva ca |
daivo vistaraśaḥ prokta āsuraṃ pārtha me śṛṇu || 6 ||
verses.word_meanings: dvau—two; bhūta-sargau—orders of created beings; loke asmin—in this world; daivaḥ—the divine; āsuraḥ—the demonic; eva ca—and also; daivaḥ—the divine; vistaraśaḥ—in detail; proktaḥ—has been described; āsuram—the demonic; pārtha—O Partha; me—from Me; śṛṇu—now hear.
verses.translation: There are two orders of created beings in this cosmos: the divine and the demonic. The divine has been described in detail; now hear from Me, O Partha, regarding the nature of the demonic.
verses.meaning: Human beings fall into two psychological categories: those aligning with dharma and cosmic harmony (Daiva), and those pursuing egoistic self-aggrandizement and hedonism (Asura).
verses.purport: Human beings fall into two psychological categories: those aligning with dharma and cosmic harmony (Daiva), and those pursuing egoistic self-aggrandizement and hedonism (Asura).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः |
न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते || ७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः |
न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca janā na vidurāsurāḥ |
na śaucaṃ nāpi cācāro na satyaṃ teṣu vidyate || 7 ||
verses.word_meanings: pravṛttim ca—right action to be engaged in; nivṛttim ca—prohibited action to be abstained from; janāḥ āsurāḥ—demonic persons; na viduḥ—do not know; na śaucam—neither internal/external purity; na api ca ācāraḥ—nor noble conduct; na satyam—nor truthfulness; teṣu—in them; vidyate—exists.
verses.translation: Persons of demonic temperament understand neither right engagement (Pravritti) nor right renunciation (Nivritti). Neither purity, nor righteous conduct, nor truthfulness is found in them.
verses.meaning: Demonic personalities lack moral compass. They do not know what actions uplift human character and what actions degrade it; their lives are devoid of ethical purity, spiritual discipline, and honesty.
verses.purport: Demonic personalities lack moral compass. They do not know what actions uplift human character and what actions degrade it; their lives are devoid of ethical purity, spiritual discipline, and honesty.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम् |
अपरस्परसम्भूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम् || ८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम् |
अपरस्परसम्भूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम् || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
asatyamapratiṣṭhaṃ te jagadāhuranīśvaram |
aparasparasambhūtaṃ kimanyatkāmahaitukam || 8 ||
verses.word_meanings: asatyam—without moral truth; apratiṣṭham—without foundation/cosmic law; te—they; jagat—the universe; āhuḥ—declare; anīśvaram—without a God/Supreme Ruler; aparaspara-sambhūtam—arising without divine cause / merely through chemical union; kim anyat—what else; kāma-haitukam—caused solely by lust / sexual desire.
verses.translation: They declare that the universe is without moral truth, without foundation, and without a God; that it is brought about only by mechanical union, having lust alone as its cause—what else?
verses.meaning: This verse describes the atheistic, nihilistic, and purely materialistic worldview: viewing creation as an accidental byproduct of chemical forces without divine intelligence, moral accountability (Karma), or transcendent purpose.
verses.purport: This verse describes the atheistic, nihilistic, and purely materialistic worldview: viewing creation as an accidental byproduct of chemical forces without divine intelligence, moral accountability (Karma), or transcendent purpose.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः |
प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः || ९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः |
प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
etāṃ dṛṣṭimavaṣṭabhya naṣṭātmāno'lpabuddhayaḥ |
prabhavantyugrakarmāṇaḥ kṣayāya jagato'hitāḥ || 9 ||
verses.word_meanings: etām—this; dṛṣṭim—philosophical view; avaṣṭabhya—clinging to; naṣṭa-ātmānaḥ—ruined in soul; alpa-buddhayaḥ—of petty/meager intellect; prabhavanti—they arise/flourish; ugra-karmāṇaḥ—engaged in cruel, violent deeds; kṣayāya—for the destruction; jagataḥ—of the world; ahitāḥ—as malevolent enemies.
verses.translation: Clinging to this nihilistic perspective, these ruined souls of meager intellect and violent deeds flourish as malevolent enemies of the world, bent on its destruction.
verses.meaning: When humans reject divine accountability and spiritual ethics, technology and power are weaponized for exploitation, warfare, and planetary devastation.
verses.purport: When humans reject divine accountability and spiritual ethics, technology and power are weaponized for exploitation, warfare, and planetary devastation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः |
मोहाद्गृहीत्वासद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः || १० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः |
मोहाद्गृहीत्वासद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
kāmamāśritya duṣpūraṃ dambhamānamadānvitāḥ |
mohādgṛhītvāsadgrāhānpravartante'śucivratāḥ || 10 ||
verses.word_meanings: kāmam—insatiable lust/desire; āśritya—taking refuge in; duṣpūram—insatiable/impossible to fulfill; dambha-māna-mada-anvitāḥ—filled with hypocrisy, pride, and arrogance; mohāt—out of delusion; gṛhītvā—holding; asat-grāhān—false concepts and unworthy values; pravartante—they act; aśuci-vratāḥ—bound to impure and unholy resolves.
verses.translation: Surrendering to insatiable lust, filled with hypocrisy, pride, and arrogance, holding false notions through delusion, they act engaged in impure and destructive vows.
verses.meaning: Lust is 'Dushpura'—a fire fed with gasoline that burns brighter with every indulgence. Demonic minds become fanatical devotees of unholy principles.
verses.purport: Lust is 'Dushpura'—a fire fed with gasoline that burns brighter with every indulgence. Demonic minds become fanatical devotees of unholy principles.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः |
कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्चिताः || ११ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः |
कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्चिताः || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
cintāmaparimeyāṃ ca pralayāntāmupāśritāḥ |
kāmopabhogaparamā etāvaditi niścitāḥ || 11 ||
verses.word_meanings: cintām—anxiety and mental turmoil; aparimeyām—immeasurable/boundless; ca—and; pralaya-antām—ending only with cosmic destruction or death; upāśritāḥ—harboring/beset with; kāma-upabhoga-paramāḥ—holding sensual indulgence as the supreme goal of life; etāvat iti—that this is all there is; niścitāḥ—firmly convinced.
verses.translation: Beset with immeasurable anxieties that end only with death, regarding sensual indulgence as their supreme goal, convinced that this material gratification is all there is;
verses.meaning: Because their desires are endless and fragile, materialists live in constant, crushing anxiety (Chinta) until their final breath, trapped in the illusion that sensual pleasure is life's only purpose.
verses.purport: Because their desires are endless and fragile, materialists live in constant, crushing anxiety (Chinta) until their final breath, trapped in the illusion that sensual pleasure is life's only purpose.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः |
ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान् || १२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः |
ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान् || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
āśāpāśaśatairbaddhāḥ kāmakrodhaparāyaṇāḥ |
īhante kāmabhogārthamanyāyenārthasañcayān || 12 ||
verses.word_meanings: āśā-pāśa-śataiḥ—by hundreds of nooses of craving and expectations; baddhāḥ—bound fast; kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ—wholly dedicated to lust and wrath; īhante—they strive; kāma-bhoga-artham—for the gratification of sensual desires; anyāyena—by unjust and unlawful means; artha-sañcayān—accumulation of wealth.
verses.translation: Bound by hundreds of tight ropes of selfish craving, wholly devoted to lust and anger, they strive to amass hoardings of wealth by unjust and corrupt means for the gratification of their senses.
verses.meaning: Craving turns into an enslaving noose (Asha-pasha). To feed their limitless desires, people resort to corruption, theft, exploitation, and injustice.
verses.purport: Craving turns into an enslaving noose (Asha-pasha). To feed their limitless desires, people resort to corruption, theft, exploitation, and injustice.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् |
इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम् || १३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् |
इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम् || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
idamadya mayā labdhamimaṃ prāpsye manoratham |
idamastīdamapi me bhaviṣyati punardhanam || 13 ||
verses.word_meanings: idam—this; adya—today; mayā—by me; labdham—has been gained; imam—this; prāpsye—I shall obtain; manaḥ-ratham—cherished desire of mind; idam—this; asti—is mine; idam api—this also; me—for me; bhaviṣyati—shall be; punaḥ—again; dhanam—wealth.
verses.translation: They boast: 'This has been gained by me today; this desire I shall soon fulfill; this wealth is already mine, and that additional treasure shall also become mine in the future.
verses.meaning: Verses 13–15 depict the internal monologue of the megalomaniacal ego: an endless obsession with hoarding, expanding financial dominance, and self-glorification.
verses.purport: Verses 13–15 depict the internal monologue of the megalomaniacal ego: an endless obsession with hoarding, expanding financial dominance, and self-glorification.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि |
ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी || १४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि |
ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
asau mayā hataḥ śatrurhaniṣye cāparānapi |
īśvaro'hamahaṃ bhogī siddho'haṃ balavānsukhī || 14 ||
verses.word_meanings: asau—that; mayā—by me; hataḥ—has been slain; śatruḥ—enemy; haniṣye—I shall slay/destroy; ca—and; aparān api—others also; īśvaraḥ aham—I am the sovereign lord/controller; aham—I; bhogī—the enjoyer; siddhaḥ aham—I am accomplished and successful; balavān—mighty and powerful; sukhī—happy.
verses.translation: 'That enemy has been eliminated by me, and others also I shall destroy! I am the sovereign ruler; I am the supreme enjoyer; I am accomplished, mighty, and happy!
verses.meaning: The ultimate delusion of the ego: declaring oneself as Ishvara (God / supreme controller), reveling in the destruction of rivals, and claiming absolute mastery over life.
verses.purport: The ultimate delusion of the ego: declaring oneself as Ishvara (God / supreme controller), reveling in the destruction of rivals, and claiming absolute mastery over life.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया |
यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः || १५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया |
यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
āḍhyo'bhijanavānasmi ko'nyo'sti sadṛśo mayā |
yakṣye dāsyāmi modiṣya ityajñānavimohitāḥ || 15 ||
verses.word_meanings: āḍhyaḥ—wealthy; abhijanavān—of noble/elite lineage; asmi—I am; kaḥ anyaḥ asti—who else is there; sadṛśaḥ mayā—equal to me; yakṣye—I shall perform lavish rituals; dāsyāmi—I shall give charity (for fame); modiṣye—I shall rejoice; iti—thus; ajñāna-vimohitāḥ—deluded by sheer ignorance.
verses.translation: 'I am wealthy and of aristocratic lineage! Who else is equal to me? I will perform grand rituals, I will give charity for fame, I will rejoice!' Thus are they thoroughly deluded by ignorance.
verses.meaning: Even religious practices and philanthropy are corrupted by the demonic ego into tools for social prestige, pride, and self-celebration.
verses.purport: Even religious practices and philanthropy are corrupted by the demonic ego into tools for social prestige, pride, and self-celebration.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः |
प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ || १६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः |
प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
anekacittavibhrāntā mohajālasamāvṛtāḥ |
prasaktāḥ kāmabhogeṣu patanti narake'śucau || 16 ||
verses.word_meanings: aneka-citta-vibhrāntāḥ—bewildered by myriad conflicting anxieties; moha-jāla-samāvṛtāḥ—ensnared in the web of delusion; prasaktāḥ—obsessively addicted; kāma-bhogeṣu—to the indulgence of sensual pleasures; patanti—they fall; narake aśucau—into a foul and tormenting hell.
verses.translation: Bewildered by countless conflicting thoughts, ensnared in the net of delusion, and addicted to the gratification of lust, they plummet into a foul and tormenting hell.
verses.meaning: The inevitable psychological and karmic outcome: Fragmented mental chaos, entrapment in self-delusion, and descent into hellish states of consciousness and suffering.
verses.purport: The inevitable psychological and karmic outcome: Fragmented mental chaos, entrapment in self-delusion, and descent into hellish states of consciousness and suffering.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः |
यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् || १७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः |
यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ātmasambhāvitāḥ stabdhā dhanamānamadānvitāḥ |
yajante nāmayajñaiste dambhenāvidhipūrvakam || 17 ||
verses.word_meanings: ātma-sambhāvitāḥ—self-conceited / thinking highly of themselves; stabdhāḥ—obstinate and arrogant; dhana-māna-mada-anvitāḥ—puffed up with wealth, prestige, and pride; yajante—they perform sacrifices; nāma-yajñaiḥ—sacrifices in name only; te—they; dambhena—out of ostentation/hypocrisy; avidhi-pūrvakam—without regard for scriptural injunctions.
verses.translation: Self-conceited, obstinate, puffed up with the intoxication of wealth and prestige, they perform ostentatious sacrifices in name only, driven by hypocrisy and disregarding scriptural rules.
verses.meaning: Ostentatious religious ceremonies performed without surrender or scriptural adherence are empty rituals that only inflate the ego.
verses.purport: Ostentatious religious ceremonies performed without surrender or scriptural adherence are empty rituals that only inflate the ego.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः |
मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः || १८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः |
मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ahaṅkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ |
māmātmaparadeheṣu pradviṣanto'bhyasūyakāḥ || 18 ||
verses.word_meanings: ahaṅkāram—false egotism; balam—brute power/coercion; darpam—insolence/haughtiness; kāmam—lust; krodham ca—and wrath; saṃśritāḥ—taking shelter of; mām—Me (the Supreme Divine); ātma-para-deheṣu—in their own bodies and in the bodies of others; pradviṣantaḥ—blaspheming and hating; abhyasūyakāḥ—finding fault through malicious envy.
verses.translation: Taking refuge in egotism, brute force, arrogance, lust, and wrath, these envious people hate and blaspheme Me, who dwell as the indwelling Lord within their own bodies and in the bodies of others.
verses.meaning: To abuse, exploit, or demean living beings is to directly insult the Divine Paramatman residing in every heart.
verses.purport: To abuse, exploit, or demean living beings is to directly insult the Divine Paramatman residing in every heart.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु नराधमान् |
क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु || १९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु नराधमान् |
क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tānahaṃ dviṣataḥ krūrānsaṃsāreṣu narādhamān |
kṣipāmyajasramaśubhānāsurīṣveva yoniṣu || 19 ||
verses.word_meanings: tān—them; aham—I; dviṣataḥ—hateful and envious; krūrān—cruel and vicious; saṃsāreṣu—in the cycles of worldly existence; nara-adhamān—the lowest among humans; kṣipāmi—I cast; ajasram—perpetually/continually; aśubhān—inauspicious and corrupt; āsurīṣu eva yoniṣu—into demonic wombs alone.
verses.translation: These cruel, hateful, and lowest of men, perpetually engaged in malicious deeds, I cast repeatedly into the cycles of rebirth within demonic wombs.
verses.meaning: By cosmic spiritual law, persistent malice and cruelty attract corresponding lower karmic trajectories, plunging degraded souls into wombs reflecting their violent consciousness.
verses.purport: By cosmic spiritual law, persistent malice and cruelty attract corresponding lower karmic trajectories, plunging degraded souls into wombs reflecting their violent consciousness.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आसुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि |
मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम् || २० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आसुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि |
मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम् || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
āsurīṃ yonimāpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani |
māmaprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yāntyadhamāṃ gatim || 20 ||
verses.word_meanings: āsurīm yonim—demonic wombs/species; āpannāḥ—having attained; mūḍhāḥ—deluded fools; janmani janmani—birth after birth; mām aprāpya eva—failing to reach Me; kaunteya—O son of Kunti (Arjuna); tataḥ—then; yānti—they go; adhamām gatim—to the lowest depths of degradation.
verses.translation: Trapped in demonic species and deluded birth after birth, failing ever to attain Me, O son of Kunti, they sink further down to the lowest depths of existence.
verses.meaning: Spiritual blindness compounds across lifetimes if uncorrected. When one continuously rejects the light of God, one descends further into darkness.
verses.purport: Spiritual blindness compounds across lifetimes if uncorrected. When one continuously rejects the light of God, one descends further into darkness.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः |
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् || २१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः |
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ |
kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet || 21 ||
verses.word_meanings: tri-vidham—threefold; narakasya—of hell / self-ruin; idam—this; dvāram—gate/portal; nāśanam ātmanaḥ—leading to the destruction of the soul; kāmaḥ—lust; krodhaḥ—anger; tathā—as well as; lobhaḥ—greed; tasmāt—therefore; etat trayam—these three; tyajet—one must abandon.
verses.translation: Three are the gates of this hell that cause the ruin of the soul: Lust (Kāma), Anger (Krodha), and Greed (Lobha). Therefore, one must resolutely abandon these three.
verses.meaning: This is one of the Gita's immortal ethical imperatives: Kama (selfish craving), Krodha (rage when desires are thwarted), and Lobha (insatiable hoarding) are the three deadly portals to ruin. Eliminating them is mandatory for spiritual salvation.
verses.purport: This is one of the Gita's immortal ethical imperatives: Kama (selfish craving), Krodha (rage when desires are thwarted), and Lobha (insatiable hoarding) are the three deadly portals to ruin. Eliminating them is mandatory for spiritual salvation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः |
आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् || २२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः |
आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
etairvimuktaḥ kaunteya tamodvāraistribhirnaraḥ |
ācaratyātmanaḥ śreyastato yāti parāṃ gatim || 22 ||
verses.word_meanings: etaiḥ—from these; vimuktaḥ—liberated; kaunteya—O son of Kunti; tamaḥ-dvāraiḥ—gates to darkness/ignorance; tribhiḥ—by three; naraḥ—a person; ācarati—practices/executes; ātmanaḥ—for the Self; śreyaḥ—what is highest good/auspicious; tataḥ—thereafter; yāti—attains; parām gatim—the supreme transcendental goal.
verses.translation: A person who is liberated from these three gates to darkness, O son of Kunti, practices what is truly auspicious for his soul, and thereby attains the supreme goal.
verses.meaning: When the mind is cleansed of lust, anger, and greed, inner spiritual intuition awakens, allowing one to pursue Shreyas (ultimate spiritual welfare) and achieve supreme liberation.
verses.purport: When the mind is cleansed of lust, anger, and greed, inner spiritual intuition awakens, allowing one to pursue Shreyas (ultimate spiritual welfare) and achieve supreme liberation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः |
न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम् || २३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः |
न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम् || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yaḥ śāstravidhimutsṛjya vartate kāmakārataḥ |
na sa siddhimavāpnoti na sukhaṃ na parāṃ gatim || 23 ||
verses.word_meanings: yaḥ—whoever; śāstra-vidhim—the ordinances and wisdom of sacred scriptures; utsṛjya—casting aside/discarding; vartate—acts/lives; kāma-kārataḥ—under the impulse of personal whimsical desire; na—not; saḥ—he; siddhim—perfection/fulfillment; avāpnoti—attains; na sukham—nor happiness; na parām gatim—nor the supreme transcendental goal.
verses.translation: He who casts aside the ordinances of sacred scriptures and acts under the impulse of whimsical desire attains neither spiritual perfection, nor true happiness, nor the supreme goal.
verses.meaning: Scripture is the collective wisdom of enlightened seers. Rejecting moral guidelines in favor of raw impulse leads to psychological frustration, social misery, and spiritual failure.
verses.purport: Scripture is the collective wisdom of enlightened seers. Rejecting moral guidelines in favor of raw impulse leads to psychological frustration, social misery, and spiritual failure.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ |
ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि || २४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ |
ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tasmācchāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ te kāryākāryavyavasthitau |
jñātvā śāstravidhānoktaṃ karma kartumihārhasi || 24 ||
verses.word_meanings: tasmāt—therefore; śāstram—the sacred scriptures (Shastras); pramāṇam—standard authority/criterion; te—for you; kārya-akārya-vyavasthitau—in determining what ought to be done and what ought not to be done; jñātvā—knowing/understanding; śāstra-vidhāna-uktam—declared by scriptural injunctions; karma—duty/action; kartum—to perform; iha—in this world; arhasi—you ought to.
verses.translation: Therefore, let the scriptures (Shastras) be your standard authority in determining what should be done and what should not be done. Understanding the duty declared by scriptural injunctions, you should perform your actions here in this world.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna concludes Chapter 16 by establishing Shastra-Pramana (scriptural authority). By aligning one's intellect with eternal Vedic wisdom, one acts without egoic attachment and navigates life with clarity, righteousness, and divine purpose.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna concludes Chapter 16 by establishing Shastra-Pramana (scriptural authority). By aligning one's intellect with eternal Vedic wisdom, one acts without egoic attachment and navigates life with clarity, righteousness, and divine purpose.
